390	    def upstream(self, v, w):
391	        """v ⇝ w (D3.3 as fixed in area 1): components j_1..j_n and ports u_1..u_n with v ∈ V_{j_1} ∖ {u_1},
392	        Out(u_i, j_i) for every i ≤ n, u_i ∈ V_{j_{i+1}} ∖ {u_{i+1}} for i < n, and u_n = w."""
393	        org = self.org
394	        # frontier of (port u reached as an output of some component, having entered from a port ≠ u)
395	        start = set()
396	        for j in org.comps:
397	            if v in org.foot[j]:
398	                for u in org.foot[j]:
399	                    if u != v and self.output(u, j):
400	                        start.add(u)
401	        seen, todo = set(start), list(start)
402	        while todo:
403	            u = todo.pop()
404	            for j in org.comps:
405	                if u in org.foot[j]:
406	                    for u2 in org.foot[j]:
407	                        if u2 != u and u2 not in seen and self.output(u2, j):
408	                            seen.add(u2)
409	                            todo.append(u2)
410	        return w in seen

412	    def families(self, C, reading):
413	        org = self.org
414	        return {
415	            "causal": sorted(j for j in org.comps if self.causal(j, C, reading)),
416	            "meas": sorted((j, m) for j in org.comps for m in org.foot[j] if self.meas(j, m, C, reading)),
417	            "rule": sorted(j for j in org.comps if self.rule(j, C)),
418	        }

662	def slot(cand, k, reading=None):
663	    """Slot_C(ℰ, k) (D6.3). Only for a port-reading query [I82]. Boundary coordinates are components here
664	    [I79]. reading "registered": exact slice at every pair, a ⊥ pair makes k no slot [I24, I83];
665	    reading "area2": [I24 (b), I83 (b); A2-01] — the relation by itself fixes the answer port to the
666	    target's answer at every pair of C where that answer is determined; the quantifier is A2-02."""
667	    reading = reading or NC1_READING
668	    p, E = cand.p, cand.E
669	    if getattr(p.Q, "kind", None) != "port":
670	        return False
671	    w = cand.deltaE
672	    if w not in E.foot[k]:
673	        return False
674	    if reading == "registered":
675	        for (a, b) in p.C:
676	            y = p.ans(a, b)
677	            if y is BOT:
678	                return False
679	            if E.L(k, cand.tau[a], cand.sigma[b]) != slice_rel(E, k, w, y):
680	                return False

684	    if not det:
685	        return False

688	            return False
689	        vals = set(t[i] for t in E.L(k, cand.tau[a], cand.sigma[b]))
690	        if vals != {p.ans(a, b)}:
691	            return False
692	    return True

838	def conflict(c1, c2, a, b, table=None, witness=False):
839	    """Conf(ℰ, ℰ'; a, b) (D8.2)."""

841	        return False
842	    y1, y2 = c1.ans_E(c1.tau[a], c1.sigma[b]), c2.ans_E(c2.tau[a], c2.sigma[b])
843	    if y1 != y2:

1618	class Hist:
1619	    """A history for provenance, with Θ supplied by hand [I90]: occurrences, which of them represent
1620	    which items ('t', 'H', 'surv', 'cod' = the codomain), which pairs occur, whether Θ admits the
1621	    population's members, and the primitive Prepares of construction traces (I56)."""
1622	
1623	    def __init__(self, occ, rep, occurs, admitted=True, prepares=False, contracts=None, records=None):
1624	        self.occ, self.rep, self.occurs, self.admitted, self.prepares = occ, set(rep), set(occurs), admitted, prepares
1625	        # [owner S41: Q6] q(o) per occurrence, in the order of occ (None: one contract throughout), and whether
1626	        # the change of contract into each occurrence, if any, carries a provenance record (D13.8, I165)
1627	        self.contracts, self.records = contracts, records

1629	
1630	# ---- Episodes (D13.8) [owner S41: Q6; I165] --------------------------------------------------------------
1631	# An episode is a subhistory in which every change of contract carries a provenance record, and which need
1632	# hold no change of contract. "L55" keeps L55 as text 104 words it (a history in which contracts change):
1633	# at least one change, each recorded. Θ by hand (I90): q(o) and the records are supplied.
1634	EPISODE_READINGS = ("S41", "L55")
1635	EPISODE_READING = "S41"

1638	def episode(qs=None, recs=None, reading=None):
1639	    """Episode(h') on a chain o_1 ≺ … ≺ o_n: qs[i] the contract operative at o_i, recs[i] whether the change
1640	    into o_i (from o_(i-1)), if there is one, carries its provenance record [I165]."""
1641	    reading = reading or EPISODE_READING
1642	    chg = [i for i in range(1, len(qs))] if qs else []
1643	    chg = [i for i in chg if qs[i] != qs[i - 1]]
1644	    if any(not (recs and recs[i]) for i in chg):
1645	        return False
1646	    return bool(chg) if reading == "L55" else True

1648	
1649	def chain_eps(qs, recs, reading=None):
1650	    """(i, o) -> Episode of the sub-chain o_i ≺ … ≺ o_o, for Con in prov_fixed_points."""
1651	    return lambda i, o: episode(qs[i:o + 1] if qs else None, recs[i:o + 1] if recs else None, reading)

1654	def faithful_on(cand, H):
1655	    """Faithful_H (D5.7): (F1) and the valuation equation of (F2) at every pair of H, and Hom(τ), which is
1656	    a condition on τ as a whole and is not vacuous when H is empty (I18)."""
1657	    return all(cand.translates(*x) and F1_at(cand, *x) and F2eq_at(cand, *x) for x in H) and hom(cand)

1660	def prepares_of(h, name):
1661	    """Whether a construction trace in h prepares the transport `name` (Prepares, I56): h.prepares is a
1662	    bool (it prepares the transport in question) or a set of transport names."""
1663	    return h.prepares if isinstance(h.prepares, bool) else name in h.prepares

1666	def sel(cand, H, h, pop_admitted=True, cod="cod", round2=False, i161=True):
1667	    """Sel(t; {t}, id, H) (D12.1, I52): H ⊆ C, its pairs occur in h, t faithful on H, members admitted,
1668	    no occurrence of h represents t, H or the survival condition. Area 1 fix (D12.1', settles H05 at
1669	    L195, as L13, L201, L411 state): nor the organization t carries to (tag `cod`). Second check (R1,
1670	    I161): and no construction trace in h prepares t. round2=True gives D12.1 as written in round 2.
1671	    Tags are Θ by hand (I90); FC12.new1 and FC83 compute Rep instead (prov_fixed_points)."""
1672	    if not set(H) <= set(cand.p.C) or not set(H) <= h.occurs:

1675	        return False

1686	    represented target in an episode of h (D13.8) [owner S41: Q6]: a sub-chain of h ending at its last
1687	    occurrence, which need hold no change of contract (reading "S41"; "L55": L55 as text 104 words it)."""

1701	# ---- Second check (R1, R3): provenance with Rep computed, not tagged -----------------------------------
1702	# A chain history o1 ≺ … ≺ on, one content c (the codomain of the transport held at the output on).
1703	# held[o]: Org_ℓ(o) has a faithful transport to c (Held, through Θ, no provenance); at the output it is
1704	# computed from t's own faithfulness. trace[o]: a construction trace in the history prepares o's transport.
1705	# selc[o]: Sel's conditions other than its exclusions (population, μ, H occurring, Faithful_H, admitted);
1706	# at the output computed from t. Rep is every fixed point R of R = {o : held[o] ∧ (Sel(o) ∨ Con(o))}.
1707	# Readings of 'represented' inside Sel, Con, Build (D18.1, I146, I162):
1708	#   U  as worded: (R) throughout, o's own occurrence in its history and episode;
1709	#   K  staged: (R) only at o' ≺ o, in Sel, Con and Build;
1710	#   T  Held in Con and Build (o' ⪯ o), and Held at o' ≺ o as Sel's exclusion;
1711	#   T' Held in Con and Build (o' ⪯ o); Sel's exclusion Rep at o' ≺ o (staged along ≺_h) [I162, the cut ruled].
1712	# i161: Sel also asks that no construction trace in the history prepares the transport [I161].
1713	PROV_READINGS = ("U", "K", "T", "T'")
1714	PROV_READING = "T'"
1715

1717	def _con_at(o, held, trace, rd, R, eps=None):
1718	    """Con at o: a trace prepares o's transport and, in some episode o_i ≺ … ≺ o (D13.8), the target is
1719	    represented as the reading has it [owner S41: Q6]. eps None: every sub-chain is an episode (one contract
1720	    throughout), and Con is as in the second check (i = 0 gives the widest range)."""
1721	    if not trace[o]:
1722	        return False
1723	    for i in range(o + 1):
1724	        if eps is not None and not eps(i, o):
1725	            continue
1726	        if rd == "U":
1727	            ok = any(x in R for x in range(i, o + 1))
1728	        elif rd == "K":
1729	            ok = any(x in R for x in range(i, o))
1730	        else:
1731	            ok = any(held[x] for x in range(i, o + 1))
1732	        if ok:
1733	            return True
1734	    return False

1737	def _prov_step(n, held, trace, selc, rd, i161, R, eps=None):
1738	    out = {}
1739	    for o in range(n):
1740	        before, upto = range(o), range(o + 1)
1741	        c_ = _con_at(o, held, trace, rd, R, eps)
1742	        if rd == "U":
1743	            s_ = selc[o] and not any(x in R for x in upto)
1744	        elif rd == "K":
1745	            s_ = selc[o] and not any(x in R for x in before)
1746	        elif rd == "T":
1747	            s_ = selc[o] and not any(held[x] for x in before)
1748	        else:
1749	            s_ = selc[o] and not any(x in R for x in before)
1750	        if i161:
1751	            s_ = s_ and not trace[o]
1752	        out[o] = (bool(s_), bool(c_))
1753	    return out
1754

1756	def build_at(n, held, trace, rd, R, o):
1757	    """Build at o (D13.3): a construction trace whose output o is a represented organization, 'represented'
1758	    read as the cut reads it (ExplUse, BindingConstruction, Owned, ¬TransferComposite set to hold, I56)."""
1759	    if not trace[o]:
1760	        return False
1761	    if rd == "U":
1762	        return o in R
1763	    if rd == "K":
1764	        return any(x in R for x in range(o))
1765	    return bool(held[o])

1768	def prov_fixed_points(n, held, trace, selc, rd, i161=True, eps=None):
1769	    """Every fixed point: a list of (R, {o: (Sel, Con)}). eps: episodes of the chain (chain_eps) [owner S41: Q6]."""
1770	    fps = []
1771	    for bits in itertools.product([0, 1], repeat=n):
1772	        R = frozenset(o for o in range(n) if bits[o])
1773	        sc = _prov_step(n, held, trace, selc, rd, i161, R, eps)
1774	        if frozenset(o for o in range(n) if held[o] and (sc[o][0] or sc[o][1])) == R:
1775	            fps.append((R, sc))
1776	    return fps

1780	    return [{"o%d" % (o + 1): "+".join(k for k, f in zip(("Sel", "Con"), sc[o]) if f) for o in sorted(R)} for R, sc in fps]

1789	    """SelResp(t -> t2; x) (D12.8 as fixed in area 1): Sel(t) on H, Viol(t; x) (a response to a violation,
1790	    L225), t2 ∈ μ⁺(t) (μ acts at least once), and Sel(t2) on H ∪ {x} in t2's history. round2=True gives D12.8
1791	    as written in round 2: Sel(t) on H, t2 ∈ μ*(t), t2 survives on H ∪ {x} (Faithful), no violation asked."""
1792	    def plus(t0):
1793	        seen, todo = set(), [t0]
1794	        while todo:
1795	            u = todo.pop()
1796	            for v in mu.get(u, ()):
1797	                if v not in seen:
1798	                    seen.add(v)

1800	        return seen

1803	        return sel(t, H, h, round2=True) and t2.name in star and faithful_on(t2, list(H) + [x])

33	def ev(f, v):
34	    if isinstance(f, str):
35	        return v[f]

37	        return not ev(f[1], v)

62	def canon(f):
63	    """The structural reading [I87]: double negations removed, conjunctions flattened and their
64	    conjuncts sorted. Logical equivalence is not used (L397)."""
65	    if isinstance(f, str):
66	        return f
67	    if f[0] == "not":
68	        g = canon(f[1])
69	        if isinstance(g, tuple) and g[0] == "not":
70	            return g[1]
71	        return ("not", g)
72	    if f[0] == "and":
73	        cs = []
74	        for g in f[1:]:

77	                cs.extend(g[1:])

208	def usable_step(j, u, memo=None):
209	    """(K2) with Live through a step strictly below u (D9.4, D9.6, I40): recursion on height."""
210	    memo = {} if memo is None else memo
211	    if id(u) in memo:

226	def usable(j, alpha, reading=None):

233	    memo = {}

240	    steps = alpha.steps()
241	
242	    def F(U):
243	        out = set()
244	        for u in steps:

248	                out.add(id(u))
249	        return out

251	    lo = set()
252	    while True:
253	        n = F(lo)
254	        if n == lo:

258	    while True:

def fc72(S):
    phi = "acc"
    a1 = Step("AndE", Not(phi), [Leaf(And(Not(phi), "q"))])
    ok_a = not rules_out(a1, phi)
    rec = Leaf("r", "record", made_from="psi")
    a2 = Step("MP", "psi", [rec, Leaf(Imp("r", "psi"))])
    ok_b = not rules_out(a2, Not("psi"))
    a3 = Step("MP", Not(phi), [Leaf("r"), Leaf(Imp("r", Not(phi)))])
    ok_c = rules_out(a3, phi)
    parts = [computed("(a), (b), (c)", "(a) ¬φ a conjunct of a leaf blocks; (b) a record made from ψ does not rule out ¬ψ; (c) r and r → ¬Acc rule out Acc",
                      ok_a and ok_b and ok_c, "(a) %s; (b) %s; (c) %s" % (ok_a, ok_b, ok_c), ["I87", "I89"])]
    # [owner S41: Q23] a premise alone is an argument (D9.2, D9.6, D9.7; I166)
    PM, design = "PM", "design"
    psi = Not(PM)  # 'perpetual motion is impossible', taken as given
    phi_d = And(design, PM)  # 'this design runs and gives perpetual motion'
    j = Assessor(["MP"], [psi])
    bare = Leaf(psi)
    args_d = enumerate_args([psi])
    ok_d = usable(j, bare) and rules_out(bare, phi_d) and any(isinstance(a_, Leaf) for a_ in X(j, phi_d, args_d))
    r2 = usable(j, bare, reading="I88")
    parts.append(computed("(d) owner S41, Q23: a premise alone rules out a design", "ψ alone, ψ ∈ Accepted_j, Incons(φ, ψ), ¬φ no conjunct of ψ ⇒ ψ ∈ X_j(φ): ψ = ¬PM ('perpetual motion is impossible'), φ = design ∧ PM",
                          ok_d and not r2,
                          "%s\nusable by j (who accepts ¬PM): %s; rules out design ∧ PM: %s; in X_j(design ∧ PM) over %d arguments (the premise alone among them): %s. "
                          "Under round 2's reading (I88: an argument has a step) the premise alone is no argument: usable %s."
                          % (bare.show(2), usable(j, bare), rules_out(bare, phi_d), len(args_d), ok_d, r2), ["I87", "I88", "I166"]))
    ok_e = usable(j, bare) and not rules_out(bare, PM)
    parts.append(computed("(e) the block holds of a premise alone", "ψ alone with ψ = ¬φ (read structurally) does not rule out φ: ¬PM alone does not rule out PM ('p because p')",
                          ok_e, "usable: %s; rules out PM: %s" % (usable(j, bare), rules_out(bare, PM)), ["I87", "I39"]))
    j0 = Assessor(["MP"], [])
    ok_f = (not usable(j0, bare)) and not X(j0, phi_d, args_d)
    parts.append(computed("(f) a premise alone that j has not taken up is not usable (I166)", "ψ ∉ Accepted_j ⇒ ¬Usable_j(ψ alone), so ψ alone rules nothing out for j",
                          ok_f, "j accepts nothing: usable %s; |X_j(design ∧ PM)| = %d" % (usable(j0, bare), len(X(j0, phi_d, args_d))), ["I166"]))
    return parts

Interesting details in FC72 (d): "in X_j(design ∧ PM) over 1 arguments" — enumerate_args([psi]) with depth=2: premises=[¬PM]; the layer = [Leaf(¬PM)]; then stepped arguments: MP needs two distinct nodes (permutations of pairs from allnodes which has only 1 node) — none. So args = [Leaf(¬PM)] only. Fine.

Note the design is ruled out as "design ∧ PM", i.e. the claim ruled out is the conjunction, not 'Acc(ℰ)'. D9.8: "a candidate is ruled out for j when the claim that it meets (E) is". In the owner's example, the single claim rules out "a design" — the design claim. The encoding rules out design ∧ PM. Faithful enough? The owner's words: "If someone uses that one claim, alone, to rule out a design, does the single claim count as an argument?" — the maths answers: yes it's an argument (usable, RO holds). ✓.

But one gap: for the ruling out of the *candidate* (D9.8), j would need Incons('Acc(ℰ)', ¬PM) — i.e. the design's meeting (E) must itself imply PM. The encoding doesn't test that the *candidate* is ruled out; only "design ∧ PM". Nearest variant judged otherwise: α = Leaf(¬PM), φ = 'Acc(ℰ)' where Acc(ℰ) ∧ PM is contingent — Incons(Acc, ¬PM) fails ⇒ X_j(Acc) = ∅ ⇒ the candidate is not ruled out, though the owner's story has the claim "used alone to rule out a design". So the maths gives: the single claim is an argument, and it rules out the design only when the design's claim is inconsistent with it. That matches S27 ("its explanation implies perpetual motion, then that's a conflict" — conflict with a claim, D8.5) — arguably the ruling-out runs through D8.5 (ConfCl) + an argument, not X_j(Acc) directly. Is that a faithfulness gap? The owner's Q23 answer "Yes, it's an argument" is delivered by D9.2. Fine. But worth noting: ruling out the design needs the design's claim to entail PM; with φ = design ∧ PM the conjunction is doing the work. I'll note the variant.

Now, an important check for Q23: I166 — "a premise alone is usable by j exactly when j tentatively accepts it". But D9.6's leaf kinds: "Leaves are record leaves (each referring to an event...) or stated assumptions and definitions." A premise alone that is a *record leaf* — usable? usable(Leaf) checks `canon(alpha.claim) in j.accepted` — for a record leaf, Accepted_j contains claims j has taken up; a record leaf's claim is the record's interpreted claim. Hmm — D9.4 Live: "d ∈ Accepted_j(ξ)" — premises j tentatively accepts. A record leaf refers to an event; does j need to accept it? For a stepped argument, a record-leaf premise needs Live too (usable_step checks each prem: live via below-step or accepted). So even in stepped arguments, a record leaf must be accepted by j or concluded by a below step! Is that right per the text? K2: "∀d ∈ Prem(u), Live_j(d;u)" and Live: "d is the conclusion of a step of the same argument as u that is usable by j, or a premise j tentatively accepts".
